hypothesis: The parent (c006) combined CTS cluster_size=1/diameter=50 with allowing upper-tier BUF/CLKBUF cells. The upper-tier buffer allowance is the mechanism that generalizes (it gives rsz resources on both tiers), while the aggressive cluster_size=1 was flagged in earlier rounds as WNS-degrading. A conservative refinement: keep the upper-tier buffer allowance but restore CTS cluster_size to a moderate value (30) while keeping the reduced diameter (50), so we retain the TNS gain from upper-tier repair without the WNS loss from over-fragmented clock clustering.
analysis: The hypothesis held: restoring CTS cluster_size=30 while keeping diameter=50 and upper-tier BUF/CLKBUF allowance yields all-valid, positive results (total +0.349, robust +0.063). All three cases improved WNS and TNS, with ariane133-ng45 strongest (dWNS +8.9%, dTNS +25.8%), consistent with upper-tier repair resources driving TNS gain without the over-fragmentation WNS penalty. Overflow ~166–184 is modest. Next step: sweep cluster_size (20/30/40) at diameter=50 to confirm 30 is near-optimal and check whether larger diameters further reduce overflow without eroding WNS.
